lines.text: Pick as many numbers from one to one hundred as you can, but none may be double or triple another.
lines.caption: Pick as many numbers from one to one hundred as you can, but none may be double or triple another.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Today we'll turn this puzzle into a chessboard.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Today we'll turn this puzzle into a chessboard.

lines.text: We want the biggest possible subset of the numbers from one to one hundred.
lines.caption: We want the biggest possible subset of the numbers from one to one hundred.

lines.text: It can never hold two numbers where one is exactly two times, or exactly three times, the other.
lines.caption: It can never hold two numbers where one is exactly two times, or exactly three times, the other.

lines.text: What's a clash? Five and ten clash: ten is double five. Five and fifteen clash too: triple!
lines.caption: What's a clash? Five and ten clash: ten is double five. Five and fifteen clash too: triple!

lines.text: But five and twenty are fine. Twenty is four times five, and four times is allowed.
lines.caption: But five and twenty are fine. Twenty is four times five, and four times is allowed.

lines.text: Our goal: keep as many numbers as we can, with no clashing pair.
lines.caption: Our goal: keep as many numbers as we can, with no clashing pair.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our plan: sort the numbers into families that can never clash with each other.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our plan: sort the numbers into families that can never clash with each other.

lines.text: Take any number, and divide out every two and every three. What's left is its core.
lines.caption: Take any number, and divide out every two and every three. What's left is its core.

lines.text: Seventy-two is eight times nine, so its core is one. Forty is eight times five: core five.
lines.caption: Seventy-two is eight times nine, so its core is one. Forty is eight times five: core five.

lines.text: Doubling adds one more factor of two, tripling one more three. So clashes stay inside one family.
lines.caption: Doubling adds one more factor of two, tripling one more three. So clashes stay inside one family.

lines.text: A core has no two or three inside it. Thirty-three cores make thirty-three families. Start with core one.
lines.caption: A core has no two or three inside it. Thirty-three cores make thirty-three families. Start with core one.

lines.text: Put one in the corner. One step right doubles. One step up triples.
lines.caption: Put one in the corner. One step right doubles. One step up triples.

lines.text: The bottom row doubles to sixty-four. Rows above start at three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one.
lines.caption: The bottom row doubles to sixty-four. Rows above start at three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one.

lines.text: Here's the key. Two of these twenty numbers clash exactly when they're neighbors in the grid.
lines.caption: Here's the key. Two of these twenty numbers clash exactly when they're neighbors in the grid.

lines.text: Now color the grid like a chessboard, green and purple.
lines.caption: Now color the grid like a chessboard, green and purple.

lines.text: Neighbors always get different colors. So the green squares never clash with each other!
lines.caption: Neighbors always get different colors. So the green squares never clash with each other!

lines.text: Count them. Four, plus three, plus two, plus one, plus one. That's eleven green squares.
lines.caption: Count them. Four, plus three, plus two, plus one, plus one. That's eleven green squares.

lines.text: Purple has only nine. So we keep the bigger color: eleven numbers from core one.
lines.caption: Purple has only nine. So we keep the bigger color: eleven numbers from core one.

lines.text: But wait. Could some clever mix of both colors beat eleven?
lines.caption: But wait. Could some clever mix of both colors beat eleven?

lines.text: Let's cut the grid into dominoes. Each covers a clashing pair, so it keeps at most one number.
lines.caption: Let's cut the grid into dominoes. Each covers a clashing pair, so it keeps at most one number.

lines.text: Here we fit nine dominoes, with two squares left over: sixty-four and eighty-one.
lines.caption: Here we fit nine dominoes, with two squares left over: sixty-four and eighty-one.

lines.text: So core one keeps at most nine, plus two. That's eleven! We can't do better.
lines.caption: So core one keeps at most nine, plus two. That's eleven! We can't do better.

lines.text: Now the other families. Core five has ten numbers, and five dominoes cover them. So it keeps five.
lines.caption: Now the other families. Core five has ten numbers, and five dominoes cover them. So it keeps five.

lines.text: The same way, core seven keeps four, core eleven keeps four, and core thirteen keeps three.
lines.caption: The same way, core seven keeps four, core eleven keeps four, and core thirteen keeps three.

lines.text: Cores seventeen, nineteen, twenty-three and twenty-five make corner shapes of four. Each keeps two.
lines.caption: Cores seventeen, nineteen, twenty-three and twenty-five make corner shapes of four. Each keeps two.

lines.text: Corner shapes of three come from the cores twenty-nine and thirty-one. Here purple wins, two to one!
lines.caption: Corner shapes of three come from the cores twenty-nine and thirty-one. Here purple wins, two to one!

lines.text: Cores thirty-five to forty-nine are pairs. The double fits, the triple doesn't. Six pairs, one each.
lines.caption: Cores thirty-five to forty-nine are pairs. The double fits, the triple doesn't. Six pairs, one each.

lines.text: Sixteen cores, from fifty-three up, stand alone: even their double is past one hundred. Keep them all!
lines.caption: Sixteen cores, from fifty-three up, stand alone: even their double is past one hundred. Keep them all!

lines.text: Now add it up. Eleven, five, four, four and three make twenty-seven. Corners of four add eight, corners of three add four, then six, and sixteen.
lines.caption: Now add it up. Eleven, five, four, four and three make twenty-seven. Corners of four add eight, corners of three add four, then six, and sixteen.

lines.text: Twenty-seven plus eight plus four plus six plus sixteen is <short pause> sixty-one! Choice C.
lines.caption: Twenty-seven plus eight plus four plus six plus sixteen is sixty-one! Choice C.

lines.text: Here's another way to see it. Count what you must throw away.
lines.caption: Here's another way to see it. Count what you must throw away.

lines.text: Add up the dominoes we drew: nine, five, four, three, two, then eight, two and six. Thirty-nine!
lines.caption: Add up the dominoes we drew: nine, five, four, three, two, then eight, two and six. Thirty-nine!

lines.text: Each domino is a clashing pair, so it costs you at least one number.
lines.caption: Each domino is a clashing pair, so it costs you at least one number.

lines.text: So you keep at most one hundred minus thirty-nine. That's sixty-one, and our coloring gets it!
lines.caption: So you keep at most one hundred minus thirty-nine. That's sixty-one, and our coloring gets it!

lines.text: When would you pick this one? Whenever you're asked for the MOST. It proves no one can beat you.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? Whenever you're asked for the MOST. It proves no one can beat you.

lines.text: A, fifty, is what you'd get from taking fifty-one to one hundred. No clashes, but not the most.
lines.caption: A, fifty, is what you'd get from taking fifty-one to one hundred. No clashes, but not the most.

lines.text: Choice E, sixty-seven, comes from taking thirty-four to one hundred. But thirty-four and sixty-eight clash!
lines.caption: Choice E, sixty-seven, comes from taking thirty-four to one hundred. But thirty-four and sixty-eight clash!

lines.text: B, fifty-eight, is too small. We already built a set of sixty-one.
lines.caption: B, fifty-eight, is too small. We already built a set of sixty-one.

lines.text: D, sixty-four, is too many. The dominoes say sixty-one is the most.
lines.caption: D, sixty-four, is too many. The dominoes say sixty-one is the most.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Show your set works, AND show nobody can beat it.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Show your set works, AND show nobody can beat it.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same rule, but now pick from the numbers one to thirty.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same rule, but now pick from the numbers one to thirty.

lines.text: What's the most you can pick?
lines.caption: What's the most you can pick?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: With thirty numbers, core one has twelve. Six dominoes cover them, and either color keeps six.
lines.caption: With thirty numbers, core one has twelve. Six dominoes cover them, and either color keeps six.

lines.text: Core five keeps three. Core seven keeps two. Cores eleven and thirteen keep one each.
lines.caption: Core five keeps three. Core seven keeps two. Cores eleven and thirteen keep one each.

lines.text: Then five loners: seventeen, nineteen, twenty-three, twenty-five and twenty-nine.
lines.caption: Then five loners: seventeen, nineteen, twenty-three, twenty-five and twenty-nine.

lines.text: Six plus three plus two plus one plus one plus five. The answer is eighteen!
lines.caption: Six plus three plus two plus one plus one plus five. The answer is eighteen!

lines.text: The big idea: split the numbers into families that can never clash.
lines.caption: The big idea: split the numbers into families that can never clash.

lines.text: In each family, clashes are neighbors. Keep the bigger chessboard color. Then dominoes prove it is the most.
lines.caption: In each family, clashes are neighbors. Keep the bigger chessboard color. Then dominoes prove it is the most.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
